fact_text: PMEX is a regulated Pakistani exchange that gives local residents access to international commodities, currencies and indices; deposits and withdrawals are converted to PKR at the prior day's USD/PKR rate.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX charges about 0.009% of trade value per trade, plus 15% SST; including taxes, investor protection and settlement guarantee fund charges, the speaker put the all-in fee at about 0.0128%.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: Standard Capital Securities charges PKR 25 per PMEX trade plus SST of PKR 3.75, a total of PKR 28.75 in the speaker's worked example.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: NCCPL's CGT processing fee is tiered on annual traded value counted from July to June and resets each fiscal year; the speaker's example reached a slab with PKR 250 plus 15% SST.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: Capital gains tax on PMEX profits is 5% for both filers and non-filers, deducted and adjusted every day, and a later loss returns the tax previously deducted.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX marks open positions to market at each day's close, booking profit or loss by closing and re-entering at the closing price; cumulative P&L equals exit minus entry, only the timing changes.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX commodity contracts carry a month code and expire before that month, so an AU26 contract expires before August 2026; a new contract is issued about two days before expiry.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: On the PMEX margin sheet dated 18 Aug 2026 the initial margin for the standard 1 oz gold contract was 5.25% of contract value, about PKR 59,500.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: The intraday 1 oz gold contract had an initial margin of 2.75%, about PKR 31,200, against 5.25% for the standard contract; intraday contracts open and expire within the same day.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: One PMEX gold contract is one troy ounce (31.10 grams, about 2.66 tola), so each $1 move in gold changes the position's profit or loss by $1.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX gold 1 oz contracts trade in whole lots of 1, with at most 20 contracts per order at one time; the stated volume limit for the contract is 60 contracts.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX runs a netting account: layered buys merge into one average price, so a single stop-loss or take-profit applies to the whole net position, and partial exits need separate sell-limit orders.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX prices are futures prices, so spot gold quotes differ; the TradingView GC1 futures symbol tracks PMEX rates, while free TradingView data is delayed about 10 minutes.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX gold contracts come in two sizes: one ounce is described as 28.35 grams, and one troy ounce as 31.10 grams.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX gold positions can only be entered in whole lots such as 1, 2 or 3; fractional sizes such as 1.2 or 1.5 are not accepted.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: PMEX gold positions are adjusted daily to the closing price, so profit and loss is booked each day until the position is closed manually.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: The Investor Protection Fund levy is 1% of the PMEX fee.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: An SCP charge equal to 10% of the PMEX fee applies on top of the exchange fee.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: Sales tax (SST) of 15% is charged on the PMEX exchange fee and on the broker's fee in the video's fee example.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: On 18 Aug 2026 the analyst's chart showed gold at about $4,048 an ounce, while the GC1 gold futures contract showed about $4,044 on delayed data.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)

fact_text: The video's worked example uses a dollar rate of about PKR 280 per US dollar as of 18 Aug 2026.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'PMEX Course For beginners 2026 | Gold Trading, MT5 & TradingView' (YouTube, 2026-08-18)
